owned_session_identity.note: WP05 tests/adapters/claude-code/real-runtime.test.ts (claude 2.1.260, darwin): the uuid is minted by the adapter and passed as --session-id, so the coordinator knows the id before the process starts; the runtime echoes it on every record and rejects a non-uuid before starting. `--session-id` cannot be combined with `--resume` unless `--fork-session` is given, so a plain resume passes only `--resume <id>` and the conversation keeps the minted id

observed_cancellation.note: WP05 tests/adapters/claude-code/real-runtime.test.ts (claude 2.1.260, darwin): the interrupt control round-trip is verified (`{"type":"control_request","request":{"subtype":"interrupt"}}` answered with `control_response` carrying `still_queued`), and process-group termination is verified (SIGTERM to the group ended the process with exit 143 and left the group empty). Interrupting a RUNNING model turn could not be executed on this machine: the stored claude.ai OAuth session is expired, so every turn ends in ~60 ms with error authentication_failed. The requested/observed split is covered deterministically by the recorded-fixture replay

resume_session.note: WP05 tests/adapters/claude-code/real-runtime.test.ts (claude 2.1.260, darwin): `--resume <id>` reuses the id in a fresh process and the runtime reports the same session id; `--resume <old> --fork-session --session-id <new>` mints the new id; an unknown id yields a bare `No conversation found with session ID: ...` line plus a result record with subtype error_during_execution. Whether the resumed turn continues the earlier CONVERSATION needs a model turn and could not be executed here

active_turn_delivery.note: WP05 tests/adapters/claude-code/real-runtime.test.ts (claude 2.1.260, darwin): a user message written to the live process's stdin is acknowledged by the runtime (--replay-user-messages echoes it with isReplay=true) — verified. Whether the runtime injects it into the RUNNING turn or schedules it as the next one could not be observed here, and the runtime's own fields (queued_turn_count, still_queued, the advertised interrupt_cancel_queued_v1 capability) describe a queue. The adapter therefore reports submitted_to_active_turn only when the echo arrives while the turn is still active, and queued otherwise

mcp_config_injection.note: WP05 tests/adapters/claude-code/real-runtime.test.ts (claude 2.1.260, darwin): `--strict-mcp-config` is verified to suppress the user's own MCP servers (mcp_servers is [] in the init record; without it the user's servers appear). Injecting a coordinator bridge through `--mcp-config` is not exercised until WP06

sandbox_workspace_write.note: WP05 tests/adapters/claude-code/real-runtime.test.ts (claude 2.1.260, darwin) (FR042): Claude Code 2.1.260 has NO OS sandbox. Executed proof: a SessionStart hook the runtime itself launched wrote outside every --add-dir directory, wrote to /tmp, read a file outside them and reached https://example.com (HTTP 200) — identically with and without `--restricted --permission-mode plan --permission-prompts none`. What the flags do bound is the TOOL SURFACE offered to the model, which is verified (`--restricted --tools Read Glob Grep` yields exactly Glob, Grep, Read; adding Edit and Write yields exactly those five; no Bash, no Task, no WebFetch, no MCP server). That is a permission boundary, not a containment boundary, so the plan's local-development profile cannot be enforced by this runtime and a kernel-level boundary must come from the environment around the process. Separately: without `--setting-sources ''` a registered project's own .claude/settings.json SessionStart hook RAN host commands in the worker session; the adapter always passes it and the hook then did not run

model_selection.note: WP05 tests/adapters/claude-code/real-runtime.test.ts (claude 2.1.260, darwin): the `initialize` control response lists the models the runtime offers with their resolved ids and supported effort levels (default, opus[1m], claude-fable-5-1[1m], sonnet, haiku on this machine); `--model sonnet` was reflected in the session's init record as claude-sonnet-5. No model turn is needed for either

effort_selection.note: WP05 tests/adapters/claude-code/real-runtime.test.ts (claude 2.1.260, darwin): `--effort` is accepted and the runtime lists low, medium, high, xhigh, max per model in the initialize control response. An unknown value prints `Warning: Unknown --effort value ... ignoring it and using the default effort` and continues, so the adapter refuses one before spawning rather than letting it be silently mapped. The runtime never reports the EFFECTIVE effort back in any record, so what actually took effect cannot be recorded

token_usage_report.note: WP05 tests/adapters/claude-code/real-runtime.test.ts (claude 2.1.260, darwin): the result record carries `usage` (input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens) and `modelUsage`. On this machine every turn failed authentication before reaching the provider, so the only values observed were the zeros of a turn that made no API call

cost_report.note: WP05 tests/adapters/claude-code/real-runtime.test.ts (claude 2.1.260, darwin): unlike Codex, the result record does carry `total_cost_usd`, and `--max-budget-usd` exists. No turn reached the provider here, so no measured value was ever observed. The adapter reports cost as `measured` only when duration_api_ms > 0 or a non-zero token count is present, and as `unavailable` with a reason otherwise — never zero for unknown
